summary: A large South American cichlid frequently kept in aquariums. Wild fish have eye-like markings near the tail, while aquarium strains include red, tiger and albino forms; adults defend territories and can eat smaller fish.
nativeRange: Amazon basin and other tropical South American drainages.

features: Robust cichlid body with a large mouth.
Wild-type adults have ringed eye spots near the tail and dorsal fin; aquarium colours vary.
Juveniles show pale and orange wavy bands with spots on the head.

habitat.description: Slow whitewater habitats, with shelter beneath submerged branches.
habitat.diet: Fish, crustaceans, insects and some fruit or other plant material.
